newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE emirate awards power plant order to U.S. firm.
newsitem.headline: UAE emirate awards power plant order to U.S. firm.

text.p: The emirate of Ajman has awarded a build own operate transfer (BOOT) contract to an American firm to set up and manage a power station, a United Arab Emirates (UAE) newspaper said on Saturday.

The project, to help meet Ajman's increasing power needs, is the first BOOT scheme in the oil-rich UAE, al-Khaleej daily quoted Ajman Crown Prince Sheikh Ammar bin Humaid bin Rashid al-Nuaimi as saying.
He gave no further details and did not say when the deal was signed. Officials were not immediately available for comment.

Sheikh Ammar also said the northern emirate, which plans to expand its free trade zone, now home to 100 local and international firms, was studying an offer for a BOOT water desalination project from an international firm.
"The government is still studying its feasibility."

Abu Dhabi, capital of the seven-member UAE, late last year set up a committee to oversee the privatisation of its water and electricity services. It also appointed consultants to study the feasibility of privatisation.
Like its Gulf Arab neighbours, the UAE wants to reduce reliance on the dominant public sector and give private investors a bigger role.
The water and electiricity sector had taken the lion's share of UAE investments -- accounting for over seven billion dirhams ($1.9 billion) in three years.

Water consumption in the UAE, where the population is growing at around four percent annually, was expected to rise to almost 606 million gallons (2.7 billion litres) a day by the year 2015 from a curent 232.5 million. In 1995, the UAE raised power rates by 33 percent, but electricity and water are still heavily subsidised.
